title: Hologram material with scanlines, flicker and glitch bands
purpose: Render three.js meshes as an additive hologram: world-space scanlines that scroll, a facing-ratio edge, stepped flicker and sideways glitch bands in the vertex stage, all driven by one time uniform, with an integer hash so the GLSL and its JavaScript mirrors agree. Use it for sci-fi displays, projections and ghosts.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE under WebGL 2 (unsigned integer GLSL and the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createHologramMaterial
exports.summary: The transparent, additive, double-sided hologram; set uniforms.uTime every frame; an unknown option throws TypeError.

exports.name: scanlineIntensity
exports.signature: scanlineIntensity(height, time, density, speed, sharpness) -> number
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the scanline profile, 1 on a line and 0 half way between lines.

exports.name: hologramFlicker
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the stepped flicker factor in [1 - depth, 1].

exports.name: glitchOffset
exports.signature: glitchOffset(height, time, bands, rate, chance, strength, seed) -> number
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the sideways glitch offset of the band holding this height, in world units.

exports.name: HOLOGRAM_GLSL
exports.summary: GLSL integer hash, scanlineIntensity, hologramFlicker and glitchOffset.

exports.name: HOLOGRAM_VERTEX
exports.summary: Vertex stage: world position with glitch bands, InstancedMesh aware.

exports.name: HOLOGRAM_FRAGMENT
exports.summary: Fragment stage: scanlines, edge and flicker, written for additive blending.

options.name: scanDensity
options.meaning: Scanlines per world unit of height.

options.name: scanSpeed
options.meaning: Lines passing a point per second; negative scrolls down.

options.name: scanSharpness
options.meaning: Exponent of the cosine profile; higher gives thinner lines.

options.name: flickerDepth
options.meaning: Largest dimming of a flicker step.

options.name: glitchBands
options.meaning: Glitch bands per world unit of height.

options.name: glitchChance
options.meaning: Share of bands displaced at a time.

options.name: glitchStrength
options.meaning: Largest sideways displacement in world units.

options.name: opacity
options.meaning: Alpha scale of the additive output.

options.name: seed
options.meaning: Selects a different flicker and glitch sequence.

limits: Stylized, not a physical light field: additive blending only brightens, so the hologram vanishes over white backgrounds, and transparent sorting follows three.js object order. Scanlines are horizontal world-space bands; they do not follow the screen or the surface. Glitch offsets move whole vertices sideways, so coarse meshes shear in steps and the offset never splits a triangle. The edge term needs smooth normals. Nothing animates until uniforms.uTime is updated. Requires WebGL 2 for unsigned integers in GLSL. Written for three.js r155 or later; only 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Raised cosine scanline profile scrolled by time
Lowbias32-style 32-bit integer hash for flicker steps and glitch band keys
